title: Scan Data for Quick Structural Summaries and Checks
text: basic example shows solve common problem:
code: library(datascan) head(CO2) #>   Plant   Type  Treatment conc uptake #> 1   Qn1 Quebec nonchilled   95   16.0 #> 2   Qn1 Quebec nonchilled  175   30.4 #> 3   Qn1 Quebec nonchilled  250   34.8 #> 4   Qn1 Quebec nonchilled  350   37.2 #> 5   Qn1 Quebec nonchilled  500   35.3 #> 6   Qn1 Quebec nonchilled  675   39.2 cols_identify_all(CO2) #> → No columns with all unique values. #> → No bijective columns. #> → No constant columns. #> → No identified columns with missing proportion. #>  #> ── Checking if all values are unique in a column ─────────────────────────────── #> [1] NA #>  #> ── Checking if any two columns are bijective ─────────────────────────────────── #> list() #>  #> ── Checking if any column is all constant ────────────────────────────────────── #> [1] NA #>  #> ── Checking if columns with preset cut-off in missing values ─────────────────── #> [1] NA cols_nested(CO2) #> [[1]] #> [1] "Plant" "Type"  #>  #> [[2]] #> [1] "Plant"     "Treatment" concurrence_matrix(CO2, Plant, Type) #> • Diagonal shows the total number of levels for Plant at the corresponding #>   level for Type #> • Off-diagonal shows the number of common levels for Plant between the two #>   levels for Type #>               #>               Quebec Mississippi #>   Quebec           6           0 #>   Mississippi      0           6 #>    #> ℹ Concurrence matrix: 2 × 2 Type.

title: Get the concurrence matrix or table — concurrence_matrix
text: concurrence_matrix() returns symmetric numeric matrix class concurrence_mat one row one column per level group. diagonal entries give number distinct levels x observed level group, -diagonal entries give number levels x shared two corresponding levels group. names x group stored .vars attribute. concurrence_table() returns information long format tibble class concurrence_tbl, one row per pair group levels columns: <group>_1, <group>_2 Factors giving pair group levels. concurrence Number levels x shared pair. prop_in_1 Proportion levels x <group>_1 also <group>_2. prop_in_2 Proportion levels x <group>_2 also <group>_1.

title: Is variable nested within another variable? — is_nested
code: df <- data.frame(   site = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 4),   plot1 = rep(c("A1", "A2", "B1", "B2"), each = 2),   plot2 = rep(c("A1", "A2", "A1", "A2"), each = 2) ) is_nested(df$plot1, df$site) # TRUE #> [1] TRUE is_nested(df$plot2, df$site) # FALSE since A1 and A2 appear in both sites #> [1] FALSE df$id <- seq_len(nrow(df)) is_nested(df$id, df$site) # FALSE since id has all unique values #> [1] FALSE is_nested(df$id, df$site, ignore = c("constant", "bijective")) # TRUE #> [1] TRUE
